szoveg_eredeti:
The truth nev­er bows. Truth nev­er apol­o­gis­es. On 18 Jan­u­ary 1869, P J Keenan, Esq., board­ed the West In­di­an mail pack­et. He ar­rived in Trinidad on 6 Jan­u­ary. On 10 Feb­ru­ary, the Gazette pub­lished a no­tice stat­ing that he was there to in­quire in­to the state of ed­u­ca­tion.

In Note 140 of his re­port, he states that the “in­tel­lec­tu­al ne­ces­si­ties” of the in­den­tured class of Asi­at­ic im­mi­grants were “over­looked”. “The C****e’s mind was left a blank” (p.48).

David Baby­deen has since writ­ten works ti­tled “C****e Odyssey” and “C****e Moth­er.” Khal Torab­ul­ly has ar­tic­u­lat­ed the prin­ci­ples of C****etude, a cousin of Negri­tude, aimed at build­ing pride for a broad group of peo­ple scat­tered every­where.

Im­pe­r­i­al cap­i­tal­ists didn’t re­cruit in­den­tured labour­ers for their sug­ar colonies. Rather, they man­u­fac­tured masks. The en­list­ment mod­el up­root­ed hor­ti­cul­tur­ists, loom op­er­a­tors, palan­quin-bear­ers, gold­smiths, shep­herds, ship­builders, sol­diers, Su­fi saints, and swamis, with cen­turies-old iden­ti­ties and repack­aged them in­to in­dis­tin­guish­able work­ers with­out caste or her­itage.

High-caste Hin­du women left In­dia for Trinidad. That is a fact! But they left In­dia as a “c****e”. They were la­belled to re­mind them of their low­li­ness in an eth­nic hi­er­ar­chy. And they were at the bot­tom of the sug­ar colony. That is al­so a fact.

Women had greater rea­son to flee. Greater tyran­ny to flee. They left their vil­lages ear­li­er, left their hus­bands be­fore leav­ing their com­mu­ni­ties, and fi­nal­ly they left In­dia. Were they suf­fer­ers, or did they take charge of their own des­tiny?

What is cer­tain is that in­den­ture­ship turned them in­to stock char­ac­ters with for­mu­la­ic qual­i­ties that shaped who they were and nar­rowed what they could be. Mis­la­belled and de­grad­ed, they could not take on Rad­ha’s pow­er to name them­selves.

Those who sur­vived cross­ing the Kaala Paani, and those who didn’t run away, burned Ra­van in ef­fi­gy at the cli­max of their Ram­leela. They re­mind­ed their chil­dren that the colo­nial­ists, in their op­pres­sion, sur­passed even Ra­van.

On ar­rival, ex­posed and washed in col­lec­tive baths, their caste con­cerns drift­ed down the stone slabs of Nel­son Is­land, in­to the Gulf of Paria. The “janew”, that sa­cred white thread, slipped through their fin­gers down­riv­er as they show­ered them­selves in de­hu­man­is­ing baths of tears.

The Colo­nial Of­fice pa­pers, doubt­ful ethno­g­ra­phers sel­dom tell tales of rape and un­recog­nised chil­dren. In 1914, a De­mer­ara woman re­sist­ed the over­seers’ at­tempts at sex­u­al as­sault. She wound­ed him with a cut­lass. Of­fi­cials dis­missed her state­ment of case. She was im­pris­oned for five years.

On June 19, 1913, in Berbice, a celi­bate “sad­hin” was sen­tenced to death for in­fan­ti­cide. Was she raped? How does a “sad­hin” come to be with a child? The colo­nial records are blank.

These in­den­tured women stood in the sug­ar fields like banyan trees, dis­play­ing the glo­ry of their roots in their choli and orhni for all to see. Their gha­gra gath­ered at the waist with a draw­string and safe­ty pin, held high above the sap­ate mud and pierc­ing cane stalks raised in threat like the jagged edge of a beer bot­tle, while ash from the singed sug­ar­cane leaves falls on every­thing like grey snow.

LLMs gen­er­al­ly do not pri­ori­tise or cen­tre mut­ed and min­imised life worlds be­cause their train­ing da­ta comes from the broad­er in­ter­net, which his­tor­i­cal­ly re­flects Eu­ro­cen­tric records. AI bias af­fects our his­to­ri­og­ra­phy.

Colo­nial ad­min­is­tra­tors, plan­ta­tion own­ers, and ship­ping com­pa­nies con­struct­ed the records that built the Colo­nial Archive. As a re­sult, most on­line da­ta is struc­tural­ly bi­ased to­ward over­seers’ per­spec­tives, in­clud­ing ship man­i­fests, court records of “run­aways,” and eco­nom­ic ledgers.

First-hand ac­counts were erased be­cause in­den­tured women’s minds were left blank. As a re­sult, in­den­tured nar­ra­tives are sta­tis­ti­cal­ly rare in the glob­al dataset com­pared with colo­nial records.

Ex­pe­ri­ences of sys­temic rape and oth­er es­tate vi­o­lence were sup­pressed, un­der­re­port­ed, or re­framed to pro­tect the eco­nom­ic mod­el, dri­vers, and over­seers, leav­ing a very small dig­i­tal foot­print for AI to learn from.

Be­cause AI mod­els re­ly on pat­tern match­ing and sta­tis­ti­cal fre­quen­cy, their “un­der­stand­ing” of these events rests en­tire­ly on da­ta cu­ra­tion. To­day, AI ar­chi­tec­tures re­spond with an “Ob­jec­tive By­stander Tone” to hu­man prompts about the life worlds of in­den­tured women in Gol­con­da, Trinidad.

LLMs adopt a neu­tral or pas­sive tone rather than “point­ing out” the planters’ wrong­do­ing or “point­ing to” the pain of women. This hap­pens be­cause the mod­el blends a few crit­i­cal his­tor­i­cal texts with a vast sea of gen­er­alised, dis­in­fect­ed colo­nial en­tries.

A blind spot in in­ter­sec­tion­al aware­ness re­mains. Stan­dard train­ing datasets fail to cap­ture the ideo­graph­ic in­ter­sec­tion of gen­der, eth­nic­i­ty, and in­vis­i­bil­i­ty. The spe­cif­ic trau­ma of women in sug­ar colonies, who faced dis­crete ex­ploita­tion dy­nam­ics and plan­ta­tion hi­er­ar­chy, is drowned out by Eu­ro­cen­tric his­to­ries.

While the mod­el’s vast ar­chi­tec­ture con­tains knowl­edge of these events, it does not au­to­mat­i­cal­ly cen­tre the vic­tim’s per­spec­tive un­less the AI is di­rect­ed to draw on spe­cif­ic, crit­i­cal his­tor­i­cal frame­works.

Dr Fazal Ali com­plet­ed his Mas­ter's in Phi­los­o­phy at the Uni­ver­si­ty of the West In­dies. He was a Com­mon­wealth Schol­ar who at­tend­ed the Uni­ver­si­ty of Cam­bridge, Hugh­es Hall; the Provost of the Uni­ver­si­ty of Trinidad and To­ba­go; the act­ing Pres­i­dent of UTT; and the Chair­man of the Teach­ing Ser­vice Com­mis­sion. He is the Pres­i­dent of NI­HERST and an ex­ter­nal ser­vices con­sul­tant with the IDB.
